section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the psalm "Shir HaMaalos MiMaamakim" is recited during the Ten Days of Repentance, and discusses the two interpretations of "MiMaamakim" from the Zohar.
section.t: "A Song of Ascents: From the depths I called You, Hashem"1,
Behold, this psalm was instituted to be recited every day of the Ten Days of Repentance,
beginning from Rosh Hashanah2
(which is the first day of the Ten Days of Repentance),
and many discourses of Rosh Hashanah begin with this verse.
And it is brought regarding this in the discourses3,
that in the explanation of "MiMaamakim" there are two opinions in the Zohar4
Rabbi Yitzchak and Rabbi Abba,
that Rabbi Yitzchak explains "MiMaamakim" as referring to the depths of man,
that the aforementioned prayer is from the depths of man's soul5,
from the depths of the soul of King Dovid5
and likewise of every single Jew who recites this psalm,
and Rabbi Abba explains "MiMaamakim" as referring to the depths above, a hidden place above, etc.
And it continues in the maamarim6,
and behold, the explanation of "MiMaamakim" is two depths,
for this is according to the two aforementioned opinions,
and based on this it is explained that according to Rabbi Yitzchak, the depth within depth is the depth of the heart5
and according to Rabbi Abba, this is the depth of depths in the levels above.
And it continues that the primary explanation is that it refers to the levels above,
that is, that through "I called You" one reaches the aspect of depth within depth,
until one ascends to such a depth that is above the division of levels,
and from there "I called You" – is drawn – "Hashem".
And the connection between the two explanations
(for one said one thing and the other said another, and they do not disagree)
is,
that the ability to draw down from this aspect of depth which is above any category of division is through the aspect of the depth of the heart,
which comes through the service of teshuvah,
as explained in the maamarim,
and as is simply understood that this is the content of this psalm
("A Song of Ascents: From the Depths"),
the prayer of teshuvah.
